selection: All five latest reports dated 2026-09-10 through 2026-09-12 in the pinned 45-entry index; one report per security in this window.
interpretation: Observed output behavior, not a backtest or an issuer re-rating. Reported subpoints are transcribed for aggregation-only regression; they have not been validated against this repository's rubric. In particular, the shared one-point visibility rationale is a failure pattern to correct, not a conclusion to preserve in new research. No archived report is modified.

cases.missing_evidence: Recurring FAD, owner/remittance scope and normalization; future investment, entitled shares and scrip participation are not modeled.
cases.visibility_reason: The report assigns one point because funded future DPS could not be constructed despite identifiable project directions.

cases.missing_evidence: Three-year recurring coverage and normalization; future capital retention and parent remittances are not fully reconciled despite historical parent cash disclosures.
cases.visibility_reason: The report assigns one point because the constrained five-year DPS model was not completed; business guidance remains documented.

cases.missing_evidence: Normalization and the remittance bridge; annual capex and later policy/entitlement assumptions are missing from the forecast model.
cases.visibility_reason: The report assigns one point because full-year future dividends are Not Forecastable in the unfinished model.

cases.missing_evidence: Company-defined FCF is available but recurring owner cash, settlement obligations, cash deductions and parent availability are not fully reconciled.
cases.visibility_reason: The report assigns one point because five-year FAD/DPS was not constructed; operating and capex guidance is present.

cases.missing_evidence: Historical all-in cash is available but recurring FAD and current-perimeter funding/normalization have not been modeled completely.
cases.visibility_reason: The report assigns one point because precise DPS could not be supported, while acknowledging sourced capex ranges and possible share-count assumptions.
